messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated OOM and container restarts observed in inference-prod across multiple pods (kv-cache + paged-attn). Auto-escalation to eng-oncall. summary: 42 OOMs in last 5m, 6 pods crashed, 2 node flaps.
maria: seeing alerts too, dashboards showing slow memory growth on paged allocator over 24h. Not sudden spike, slow creep.
oncall-dan: I'm on it. Can someone grab recent logs from one of the crashing pods? pod name pattern: inference-serve-*-kv
sam-eng-ml: grabbing logs now, suspect allocator fragmentation + KV cache retention. posting snippet.
sam-eng-ml: ```
2026-03-15T09:41:02Z ERROR runtime: cuda alloc failed: out of memory
stack: alloc_gpu_buffer(size=1048576) -> paged_attn_allocator::alloc_page() -> kv_cache::reserve_slot()
WARN paged_attn: free_pages=128, fragmented_pages=4300, total_pages=4428
ERROR allocator: unable to find contiguous pages, fallback failed -> OOM
```
chris-sre: that fragmentation line stands out. Free pages low, huge fragmented_pages count. This matches slow creep fragmentation we've seen before.
eva-product: customer impact? any 500s surfacing to clients?
amy-cs: yes, some customers report latency spikes and `503` on streaming endpoints since ~09:35 UTC. A few reports mention partial responses. Tracking impacted tenants in cs-dashboard.
oncall-dan: quick mitigation plan: 1) route traffic away from affected nodes via LB or node selector 2) reduce max_seq / batch size for affected model route to lower memory pressure 3) clear KV cache (soft) or restart pods if needed 4) enable temporary model fallback to smaller quantized variant.
maria: I can patch route config to reduce batch size to 8 and max_seq 512 for the model group showing most OOMs. Pushing now.
deploy-bot: rollout started: config/route/inference-model-group patch -> batch_size=8, max_seq=512 (canary to 3 pods)
sam-eng-ml: also pushing allocator mitigation flag: paged_attn.enable_compaction=true (runtime flag) to canary nodes. This will run background compaction to defragment pages. Risk: small CPU spike, but helps fragmentation.
chris-sre: good. Also consider lowering kv_cache.retention_ms to 30000 temporarily. That will reduce persistent KV consumption.
maria: applied kv_cache.retention_ms=30000 to canary set. Monitoring memory graphs.
sam-eng-ml: logs from restarted pod after config: ```
2026-03-15T09:48:14Z INFO paged_attn: compaction started, reclaimed_pages=120
2026-03-15T09:48:19Z INFO kv_cache: evicted 340 entries (size=12.3MB)
2026-03-15T09:48:23Z INFO runtime: memory stabilized, rss delta=-1.1GB
```
oncall-dan: nice. How's error rate?
amy-cs: 503s dropped from ~120/min to ~8/min on impacted tenants after canary. Customers on affected routes still seeing occasional failures but much improved.
eva-product: can we do a customer-facing note? suggest status update message?
amy-cs: drafting message: "We're experiencing reduced availability on certain inference routes; mitigations applied, monitoring closely. ETA for full recovery 1h"
chris-sre: running full cluster sweep: looking for nodes with high fragmentation metric. Found node gpu-node-17 with repeated minor flaps and highest fragmented_pages. Proposing cordon + drain.
maria: preparing drain: kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=10m
deploy-bot: drain initiated on gpu-node-17. Pods rescheduled to other nodes.
sam-eng-ml: note: rescheduling can temporarily increase memory pressure elsewhere. We'll watch. If other nodes start creeping, revert eviction and instead reboot node after snapshot.
oncall-dan: agree. We'll only drain if canary shows sustained improvement. Current canary metrics look good for 12m.
chris-sre: after drain, node had a kernel dmesg entry indicating CUDA driver GPU reset attempts + nvml errors -> likely thermal or driver-level instability causing memory allocator to mis-handle. Saving logs to incident channel.
sam-eng-ml: posting kernel snippet: ```
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=2048, Graphics Reset
[  123.456801] cuda: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory
[  123.456812] paged_attn: allocator assertion: unable to coalesce fragmented pages
```
amy-cs: customers on premium tier flagged for immediate outreach. Can we confirm no model outputs leaked or partial outputs persisted?
maria: no signs of data leakage. Faults are runtime OOMs causing aborted responses.
eva-product: next steps for P0: 1) finish node drain for gpu-node-17 2) roll compaction flag to wider pool 3) schedule reboot & NV driver check for node 17 4) plan postmortem focusing on paged_attn compaction failure and kv cache retention defaults.
oncall-dan: agreed. I'm documenting action items in incident doc. Handoff to night oncall at 11:00 UTC. Leaving runbook with steps taken and config diffs.
amy-cs: I'll push the customer note and follow up with targeted outreach to impacted accounts.
chris-sre: FYI, will open infra ticket for nv driver upgrade + thermal check. Also adding longer-term mitigation: improve allocator compaction heuristics and introduce prioritized eviction for large KV entries.
sam-eng-ml: saving heap/alloc traces and metrics to s3://redwood-incidents/1798001234/ for postmortem.
maria: final check: current 5m OOMs => 1, restarts => 0. Marking incident as mitigated but not resolved. Will update incident channel when cleared. :white_check_mark:
